Subject: Post-demo: quick procurement check and next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and two asks so we can map the right commercial path:

1) Procurement readiness: you mentioned central procurement prefers PO for enterprise purchases, but engineering-to-procurement handoff can vary by BU. Can you confirm whether the pilot (first 6 months, ~$18k/mo estimate) would go on a central PO or a card (team credit card) while procurement completes paperwork?

2) Marketplace interest: you noted both AWS Marketplace & GCP Marketplace are on the table. Which is higher priority for billing integration (if any)? If you have an internal preference, we can prioritize generating a marketplace-eligible quote/contract.

Attached is a one‑pager that outlines options (direct invoice/PO, credit card, and marketplace flows) plus a draft quote for the pilot. If helpful, Marissa can run through procurement nuances and timelines with your procurement contact.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm purchase path (PO vs card) by EOD Friday, 4/30
- If PO, please share the procurement contact name and A/P email; we’ll send standard MSA + PO instructions.
- If marketplace preferred, let us know which cloud provider and we’ll produce a Marketplace SKU quote.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that’s easier.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 15:12, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and two asks so we can map the right commercial path:

Thanks Sofia — quick answers below.

- Pilot budget is owned by our AI platform team; they can pay on a card for the pilot, but procurement will require a PO for anything > $50k/year. The pilot is expected to be under that threshold, so card is acceptable short-term.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace would be ideal (we're already standardized on AWS billing for other SaaS). GCP is secondary.

Procurement contact for formal contract questions is Lisa Cheng (lisa.cheng@stellarishealth.com). I can intro if needed.

Can you confirm whether using card for pilot means we can start right away or if there are any gating legal items? Also curious whether Redwood needs any paperwork from our side to enable AWS Marketplace listing if we go that route later this year.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of AI Platform | Stellaris Health

Hi Samantha —

Great, thanks for the clarity. Quick notes on the two gating items you asked about:

1) Start with card: card payment for the pilot is perfectly fine. We can provision hosted accounts and activate them immediately once payment method is provided. No legal hold for a pilot under standard terms — we typically require the PO/MSA only when customers want invoiced billing or committed reserved capacity.

2) AWS Marketplace: to list on AWS Marketplace later in the year we’ll need a few items from your side (for marketplace-enabled billing):
   - Cloud account alias / marketplace procurement contact (for entitlements)
   - An internal procurement SLA contact for billing reconciliation (often A/P email)
   - A short seller onboarding form (we can send) — this is only required if you actually want marketplace procurement enabled on purchase; moving to marketplace later does not block the pilot.

I’ll attach the short checklist for marketplace onboarding. I can also coordinate with Karthik on timing for marketplace SKU creation and the procurement doc we'll send to Lisa.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Sofia: send a payment link for card activation + invoice detail for finance (we'll track as part of the deal).
- Samantha: intro to Lisa Cheng (procurement). If not today, by EOD Friday 4/30.
- Karthik: please flag any internal timelines or questions for marketplace enablement.

Thanks — Marissa
RevOps Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Hi all —

Thanks Samantha. Quick technical/procurement note from my side:

- If you go card-first, we'll provision API keys and a sandbox org within 24 hours after payment clears. Production access and billing reconciliation will follow once we receive a purchase order or finalize the marketplace flow.
- For AWS Marketplace specifically, timeline to get a Seller SKU live (assuming we have your procurement contact + quick onboarding form) is typically 4–6 weeks. We can parallelize SKU creation with the pilot so you can evaluate without waiting for Marketplace activation.

Sofia / Marissa: I'll prepare the Marketplace onboarding form and a short checklist for Lisa. Samantha — if you can loop in Lisa on the thread (lisa.cheng@stellarishealth.com), we'll start the paperwork in parallel and you can still pay by card to get started.
